# Tables a signed-in session (`authenticated`) can reach in a migration-built database that the role-by-table matrix
# (`tests/test_rls_role_by_table_matrix_pg.py`, `fixtures/rls_expected_access.json`) does not observe (POST-A-008).
# One table a line: its name, a tab, and `write` (the role holds INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE, at table or column level) or
# `read` (SELECT only). Measured on 15-11-2026 against the migrations up to 594: 265 tables reachable, 99 relations in the
# matrix, the 193 below outside it, 76 of them writable. Production may grant less (fixtures/tables_the_signed_in_role_cannot_write.txt
# is read from production); this list is about the migrations, which are what a fresh database and every test build.
#
# IT ONLY SHRINKS. `tests/test_every_table_a_signed_in_session_reaches_is_observed_or_named_pg.py` holds it equal to the database in
# both directions: a table that gains a grant and is neither in the matrix nor here fails (add it to the matrix, take the grant away,
# or name it here and raise the ceiling in the test, which a reviewer sees); a table that leaves the matrix's blind spot (it is added
# to the matrix, or no signed-in session reaches it any more) is deleted from here; and a `read` table that gains a write is moved
# to `write` by hand, so a widened grant is a visible diff.
